purpose: Put published measurement against growth_exp_n, the subcooling exponent, which the project lists as unfitted. This one is not a plausibility check: it changes an engineering verdict.

model_value.note: Mori (2001) dT^(3/2), convection-controlled growth -- inside the published 1.5-2.5 range.
model_value.previously: 1.0, the leading term of a power series in subcooling. Defensible as a FORM and below the range as a VALUE; the headline verdict then rested on the most favourable end of an unfitted parameter, so the default was moved.

literature.primary_source: Bhattacharjee, G., Choudhary, N., Kumar, A., Chakrabarty, S., Kumar, R. (2021), 'Diffusion-based modeling of film growth of hydrates on gas-liquid interfaces', Chemical Engineering Science 234:116417. Read directly from the open-access NSF-PAR copy (par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10232430), not from a citing summary.
literature.quoted: All of this explains how values of n ranging from 1.5 to 2.5 in DT^n_sub often accurately model experimental data (Daniel-david et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2018; Mori, 2001; Peng et al., 2007).
literature.mechanism: Their Eq. 2.11 is exponential in subcooling; the Taylor expansion (Eq. 2.12) v_f = a(e1*DT + e1^2/2*DT^2 + e1^3/6*DT^3 + ...) reproduces the whole family. n = 1 is that series truncated at its FIRST term, which is why it is defensible as a form and why it sits at the bottom of the range rather than outside it.

specific_models.Peng_2007_plus_Mori: v_f proportional to DT^(5/2), via film thickness inversely proportional to subcooling

literature.subcooling_range_of_the_data: 2 to 12 K, which brackets this case (as-operated max 6.3 C, shut-in 9.8 C)

consequence_for_this_case.source: case/outputs_steady/sensitivity_phiSH.csv, the project's own one-at-a-time sweep, as-operated duty
consequence_for_this_case.finding: The as-operated verdict 'does not plug' (P_plug = 0) holds at n = 1.0 to 1.5 within a 48 h window. Over the range published film-growth data supports (1.5-2.5), Phi_SH exceeds the derived Phi_crit = 1.08 at EVERY value, and from n = 1.75 the line plugs in 50-67 % of realisations. THE SHIPPED DEFAULT IS NOW 1.5, the floor of that range, so the headline is no longer read at a point below the measurements. Two things must be said with it. (1) 1.5 is the floor, and the published exponents are for FILM growth at a gas-liquid interface while this model grows a WALL deposit, so no value in 1.5-2.5 is established for this geometry -- the primary result stays the n-family. (2) The 48 h window matters: at n = 1.5, Phi_SH = 1.66 implies an EQUILIBRIUM deposit of 35.2 mm against a consolidation threshold of 22.9 mm, and 48 h reaches only 8.8 mm, a quarter of that equilibrium. 'Does not plug' is therefore a statement about the window, not the duty; see case/scripts/run_long_horizon.py.
consequence_for_this_case.what_is_NOT_claimed: This does not establish that the line plugs. The cited exponents are for hydrate FILM growth at a gas-liquid interface, whereas this model grows a deposit at the WALL through a_wall; the two are related but not the same geometry, and no source here measures a wall-deposit exponent on a flowing crude line. What it does establish is that n = 1 is not a neutral default: it is the value most favourable to the reported verdict, and the verdict does not survive the middle of the published range.

recommended_action: DONE. The default was moved from 1.0 to 1.5 and every artefact regenerated. What remains is to report the n-family as the primary result rather than any single point, and to state the simulated window beside any 'does not plug'.
